notes.6: In this exercise candidates are required to transfer information from the text without any kind of error or inaccuracy. Most candidates did not encounter difficulties in finding the correct information to complete the form. Candidates should ensure when writing the address that they follow the correct order i.e. first give the house number, then the apartment name, the street, and finally the city name. This year most of the candidates correctly transcribed the address. Few candidates made significant mistakes. Exercise 3 Question 7–9 The source text was about encouraging children to lead a healthy lifestyle. Most of the candidates gave correct details under the headings except for 8 which proved challenging.
notes.7: The first heading under which candidates had to come up with two points focused on the problems created by an imbalanced diet. The correct answers were: “anger and irritation” and “find it hard to get on with other children”. Most candidates managed to provide two correct points. A few candidates made ‘anger’ and ‘irritation’ two separate points and only achieved 1 mark rather than 2.
notes.8: The next heading required candidates to state what were specialists’ views about a balanced diet. The stronger candidates gave three correct points under this heading. Others only managed to provide 1 or 2 details.
notes.9: The heading here was ‘how to protect yourself from becoming overweight’. Most of the candidates gave correct details and achieved the marks. Exercise 4
notes.10: In this summary-writing exercise up to 6 marks are available for Content and up to 4 marks are available for Language. Most candidates appeared to be well prepared for the requirements of this exercise and they generally performed well. Many candidates wrote their summaries in their own words and they were, therefore, able to access the full range of marks available for Language. Most of the candidates wrote concisely, covering 5 or 6 correct points from the text. They also managed to secure 3 out of 4 marks for language; a few candidates scored full marks for language. The majority of candidates kept their answer within the word limit. However, a small number of candidates exceeded the word length requirement. Section 2 Exercise 5 Questions 11–17 This text was about a man who became a detective as he liked to know about others’ lives. Many of the candidates performed well in this exercise. Most candidates answered the true/false questions accurately and managed to supply the correct statement for the false options. From Question 15–17, most of the candidates gave accurate responses. Some candidates gave an incorrect answer to Question 15. The question was about how the fee was decided. There were two points for this answer (i) day to day (ii) according to the task. Some candidates only offered 1 point. Exercise 6 This year’s essay topic was “How an inspiring personality has affected your life.” Several candidates gave the name of the person and explained in detail why and how this person has inspired them. Others did not understand the task and gave an irrelevant answer. Summary As last year, spelling errors were the main reason for loss of marks. Firstly, the use of the vowel sound ‘Ee’ was often used incorrectly. Secondly, the aspirated letters were written with non-aspirated letters in Hindi. Thirdly, the conjunct in Hindi, especially with the letter ‘Ra’, was not used correctly. Teachers should encourage their students to think in Hindi because some sentence constructions sounded as if students were planning what they wanted to write in English and then translating their thoughts into Hindi. This caused problems with the syntax of their writing. HINDI AS A
notes.key_messages: In Exercises 1, 3 and 5 the emphasis is on reading skills. Spelling errors are tolerated provided they do not interfere with the communication of the correct answer. Candidates are not required to write in full sentences to score the marks, as long as the answer is clearly communicated. In Exercise 2, complete accuracy is required when completing all details. In Exercise 4 and Exercise 6 marks are awarded not only for content but also for accuracy of language. Therefore, it is important that candidates check their work carefully for spelling and grammatical errors.
notes.general_comments: This year the majority of candidates performed well and appeared to be well prepared for the exam format. Most candidates managed to write within the word limit where it was applicable. However, a few candidates still exceeded the word limit in Exercise 3.
